summary: Unexpected CI enumeration and token refresh spikes after user-run audit script request
description:
Issue summary: Multiple CI jobs began scanning repos and attempting service principal token refreshes after an engineer executed an attached 'audit.sh' script that arrived via an external email. Impact: Elevated token refresh activity, several failed privileged API calls, and automated rotation of a subset of Vault tokens. Potential data-plane exposure appears limited; however, multiple service principals showed anomalous TTL resets and auth noise. Environment: Production, us-east-1. Initial reporter: engineer in infra team who received an email asking for a quick audit.

Immediate impact observed:
- Spike in /v1/auth/token/refresh events in Vault between 2026-03-10T09:12 and 2026-03-10T09:38 UTC.
- Numerous CI jobs started executing ephemeral scripts that enumerated repository lists and attempted curl calls to internal service endpoints.
- 3 service principals reported refresh attempts with invalidated client secrets; 2 secrets subsequently rotated automatically by vault-rotator.

Why this is sensitive: The email contained a zip with an 'audit.sh' wrapper that executed a third-party binary. The binary initiated outbound connections and invoked our CI runner via the internal API token stored in the user's ssh-agent during a local dev-to-CI bridge operation. Triage priority: high due to privileged token churn and potential lateral movement vector.
steps_to_reproduce: Receive externally-sourced email with attachment 'quick-audit.zip' (reported sample)
User extracts and runs ./audit.sh on a workstation that has SSH agent forwarding enabled to CI runner proxy
audit.sh downloads and executes a helper binary which calls internal CI/run API with available agent credentials
CI runner executes a repo enumeration job that attempts to read secret manifests and refreshes service principal tokens via Vault API
logs: 2026-03-10T09:14:22Z vault: POST /v1/auth/token/refresh svc-pr-ci-deployer status=200 uid=svc-pr-ci-deployer ttl=3600
2026-03-10T09:15:03Z ci-runner-42: job 9876 started by user maya.cheng via api-token, step=repo-listing
2026-03-10T09:16:11Z ci-runner-42: outbound curl to https://external-helper-hosted.example.net/lookup returned 200; payload size 12KB
investigation_notes: Initial interview with reporting engineer: they confirm they clicked and ran an attachment after a contextual email claiming to be 'security audit' from a vendor. The email was not from an allowlisted vendor domain.

Observed correlation between user's local SSH agent forwarding and CI runner logs: agent socket path exposed to runner proxy via ephemeral ssh-tunnel created by developer for convenience (developer workflow).
Host-level forensic snapshots requested for the reporting machine and CI runner 42. Endpoint AV did not flag the helper binary; we uploaded sample to sandbox for analysis (job #SAND-3347).
Vault audit logs show the token refresh calls originated from ci-runner-42's IP range; source process user indicates 'runner-executor' with parent pid tied to job 9876.
comments: Aisha Patel (reporter) 2026-03-10: 'User forwarded email and ran attachment; reporting that CI started strange jobs immediately after.'
Liam O'Connor (security-ops) 2026-03-10: 'We have isolated the CI runner and taken it off the autoscaler. Requesting immediate rotation of all service principal secrets used by CI runners.'

Diego Rivera (assignee) 2026-03-10: 'Tried to reproduce with a local exec; reproduced outbound lookup to external-helper-hosted.example.net. Uploading binary to malware sandbox and creating blocklist rule at egress.'

IR Team 2026-03-11: 'Endpoint team delivered forensic bundle for reporting host; no elevated persistence found yet. Recommended rotating affected tokens and disabling ssh-agent forwarding for CI bridge workflow until patch applied.'
Infra Lead 2026-03-12: 'Raised PR to CI-runner to reject any jobs triggered from unapproved agent-forwarded sessions: PR 412.'
resolution: Mitigation actions in progress: disabled ci-runner-42 and removed it from rotation, rotated impacted service principal secrets (svc-pr-ci-deployer, svc-pr-cache-warmer), blocked external-helper-hosted.example.net at the network egress gateway, applied temporary firewall to limit Vault token refresh endpoints to internal control plane, and created emergency policy to disable ssh-agent forwarding in CI bridge. Forensics ongoing — no confirmed data exfiltration from S3 or artifact stores at time of last update. Follow-ups: complete host-level root cause analysis, expand blocklist, enforce secure developer workflows for bridging credentials, and review auto-rotate rules to avoid partial rotations.
